exact_question: Compare diffusion and osmosis in terms of concentration gradients, membrane permeability, and water movement.
actual_published_body:
Diffusion is the movement of substances from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration, and a space with a different concentration of a single substance is said to have a concentration gradient [ev_002]. Osmosis is the movement of free water molecules through a semipermeable membrane according to the water's concentration gradient across the membrane, which is inversely proportional to the solute's concentration [ev_004]. Osmosis is a special case of diffusion [ev_001].

Concentration gradients: each separate substance in a medium has its own concentration gradient, independent of the concentration gradients of other materials, and each substance diffuses according to that gradient [ev_014]. In osmosis, water has a concentration gradient in the system and diffuses down its own concentration gradient, crossing the membrane to the side where water is less concentrated [ev_008].

Membrane permeability: in diffusion across a membrane, only the material capable of getting through the membrane will diffuse through it [ev_008]. Whereas diffusion transports material across membranes and within cells, osmosis transports only water across a membrane, and the membrane limits the diffusion of solutes in the water [ev_001].

Water movement: water moves from an area of high concentration of free water molecules to one of low free water molecule concentration [ev_001]. In osmosis, water always moves from an area of higher water concentration to one of lower water concentration, and this diffusion of water through the membrane continues until the water concentration gradient goes to zero [ev_008].
actual_published_short_answer: Diffusion moves substances from higher to lower concentration along a concentration gradient [ev_002], and each substance diffuses according to its own independent gradient [ev_014]. Osmosis is a special case of diffusion in which only water crosses a semipermeable membrane, moving from higher to lower free-water concentration along the water's concentration gradient, which is inversely proportional to solute concentration [ev_001] [ev_004].

selected_own_fragments.exact_text: FIGURE 3.21 In osmosis, water always moves from an area of higher concentration (of water) to one of lower concentration (of water). In this system, the solute cannot pass through the selectively permeable membrane. A principle of diffusion is that the molecules move around and will spread evenly throughout the medium if they can. However, only the material capable of getting through the membrane will diffuse through it. In this example, the solute cannot diffuse through the membrane, but the water can. Water has a concentration gradient in this system. Therefore, water will diffuse down its concentration gradient, crossing the membrane to the side where it is less concentrated. This diffusion of water through the membrane—osmosis—will continue until the concentration gradient of water goes to zero. Osmosis proceeds constantly in living systems. scientific_scope_limit: Unqualified always and water-gradient-goes-to-zero generalize the cited ideal passive selective-membrane illustration. They are not an unrestricted thermodynamic law for systems with opposing pressure or other constraints. Inversely proportional is qualitative textbook wording, not a quantified law established here.
